## 5. Paṇihita-accha Vagga

41. "Bhikkhus, just as if a spike of hill-rice or a spike of barley is poorly directed, it is impossible that it will pierce the hand or foot, or draw blood, even if pressed by the hand or trodden by the foot. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, the spike is poorly directed. In the same way, bhikkhus, it is impossible for that bhikkhu, with a poorly directed mind, to pierce ignorance, to arouse true knowledge, and to realize Nibbāna. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, the mind is poorly directed."

In the same way, bhikkhus, it is possible for that bhikkhu, with a well-directed mind, to pierce ignorance, to arouse true knowledge, and to realize Nibbāna. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, the mind is well directed."
